finalText:
Diagnosis: the client pod is misconfigured to bypass Kubernetes DNS, so it cannot resolve the Service name; the Service/backend itself appears healthy.

- Root cause
  - `pod/c070-client` sets `dnsPolicy: None` with a custom `dnsConfig`, overriding cluster DNS.
  - Its only nameserver is `203.0.113.1` and search domain is `bad.local`, so Kubernetes Service names like `c070-server-svc` / `c070-server-svc.siclaw-eval-yye-20260602.svc.cluster.local` will not resolve via in-cluster DNS.

- Concrete evidence
  - `c070-client` pod spec:
    - `dnsPolicy: None`
    - `dnsConfig.nameservers: [203.0.113.1]`
    - `dnsConfig.searches: [bad.local]`
  - `service/c070-server-svc` is valid:
    - `selector: app=c070-server`
    - `port 80 -> targetPort 8080`
    - `clusterIP: 172.17.69.204`
  - `endpoints/c070-server-svc` is populated:
    - backend pod IP `172.16.36.208:8080`
  - `pod/c070-server` is Running/Ready with container port `8080`.

- Impact / scope
  - Directly affects `pod/c070-client` resolving Kubernetes Service DNS names.
  - No evidence in this case that `c070-server` or `c070-server-svc` is broken; backend selection and endpoint publication are working.

- Confidence
  - High.

- Safe remediation suggestion
  - Remove the custom DNS override from `c070-client` and use `dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst` (or omit DNS settings entirely).
  - If custom DNS is truly required, include the cluster DNS service IP and Kubernetes search domains so Service names still resolve.

Diagnosis: the client pod is misconfigured to bypass Kubernetes DNS, so it cannot resolve the Service name; the Service/backend itself appears healthy.

- Root cause
  - `pod/c070-client` sets `dnsPolicy: None` with a custom `dnsConfig`, overriding cluster DNS.
  - Its only nameserver is `203.0.113.1` and search domain is `bad.local`, so Kubernetes Service names like `c070-server-svc` / `c070-server-svc.siclaw-eval-yye-20260602.svc.cluster.local` will not resolve via in-cluster DNS.

- Concrete evidence
  - `c070-client` pod spec:
    - `dnsPolicy: None`
    - `dnsConfig.nameservers: [203.0.113.1]`
    - `dnsConfig.searches: [bad.local]`
  - `service/c070-server-svc` is valid:
    - `selector: app=c070-server`
    - `port 80 -> targetPort 8080`
    - `clusterIP: 172.17.69.204`
  - `endpoints/c070-server-svc` is populated:
    - backend pod IP `172.16.36.208:8080`
  - `pod/c070-server` is Running/Ready with container port `8080`.

- Impact / scope
  - Directly affects `pod/c070-client` resolving Kubernetes Service DNS names.
  - No evidence in this case that `c070-server` or `c070-server-svc` is broken; backend selection and endpoint publication are working.

- Confidence
  - High.

- Safe remediation suggestion
  - Remove the custom DNS override from `c070-client` and use `dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst` (or omit DNS settings entirely).
  - If custom DNS is truly required, include the cluster DNS service IP and Kubernetes search domains so Service names still resolve.
